name: Wall walk
movement: facing a wall, the fingers walked up it as high as is comfortable and back down

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you, the arm on the wall nearest the camera.

words.hint: Facing a wall, the fingers of one hand walked up it as high as is comfortable, then down.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Face a wall, a little less than arm’s length away, side on to the phone, fingertips on it.
words.position: Stand facing a wall about three-quarters of an arm’s length away, side on to the phone, the working arm nearest it. Fingertips on the wall at waist height, elbow a little bent.
words.top: The arm walked up the wall as high as is comfortable — aim for the arm level with the shoulder or above — the trunk tall and still, the shoulder down away from the ear.
howto: Face the wall, about three-quarters of an arm’s length away, fingertips on it at waist height, elbow slightly bent.
Walk the fingers up the wall like a spider, slowly, as high as is comfortable. The fingers do the work, not the shoulder muscles.
Hold at the top for the count. Keep the trunk tall — no leaning back — and the shoulder down, away from the ear.
Walk the fingers back down slowly, helped by the other hand if you need. The rep counts when the hand is back at waist height.
words.cannot: Whether the fingers or the shoulder muscles are doing the lifting, and whether the shoulder blade is moving well: it sees how high the arm goes, the trunk, the elbow and the shoulder rising toward the ear.
words.about: Wall walk — standing side on, facing the wall: the reach, as the angle at the shoulder between the hip and the wrist, at least 110° at the top (the arm level with the shoulder is 90; a healthy shoulder reaches 170); a rep is under way past 90 and counts when the hand is back under 40; the trunk no more than 12° back or 20° in from upright, so leaning back to gain height is called; the elbow at least 125° at the top — fingertips on the wall bend it on the way up; and the shoulder kept down, the ear-to-shoulder distance at least 78% of what it was at the start — a shrug shortens it. Hold three seconds at the top. The top is the setting to move as the shoulder frees: a physio lowers it to 100 in the early weeks and raises it as the range returns.
words.lost: Stand side on to the camera facing the wall, the whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Go to the point of stretch, not pain. Height is not the goal; a little more each week is.
words.easier: A lower top; a shorter hold; stand closer to the wall.
words.harder: A higher top; a longer hold at the top; a slow count on the way down.
words.mistakes: Leaning back to gain height; shrugging the shoulder up to the ear; bending the elbow and pushing with it; rushing.

measurements.label: arm raised
measurements.why: The angle at the shoulder between the hip and the wrist: the arm by the side is about 15, level with the shoulder 90, straight up 170. Also the progress measurement: under way past raiseAt, back when under downAt.

settings.label: Arm raised at the top, at least (90 is level with the shoulder)

measurements.label: trunk upright
measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line off vertical, + toward the wall. Leaning back (negative) is the classic cheat for height.

measurements.label: elbow nearly straight
measurements.why: Straight is 180. Judged at the top only: with the fingertips on the wall the elbow has to bend as the hand passes shoulder height, and straightens again above it.

measurements.label: shoulder down, % of start
measurements.why: The ear-to-shoulder distance against the trunk, as a percent of what it was at the start: a shrug brings the shoulder up toward the ear and shortens it. Under 85 is a shrug.

settings.label: Ear-to-shoulder distance, % of the start, at least

prompt.text: Walk the fingers up the wall

faults.label: Elbow bending
faults.text: Keep the arm long — elbow nearly straight

faults.label: Reach short
faults.text: A little higher — walk the fingers up
faults.deep: Higher if you can, to the point of stretch

faults.label: Leaning back
faults.text: Don’t lean back — stand tall and let the shoulder do the reach
faults.deep: You are leaning back for height — come upright, even if the hand comes down

faults.label: Leaning in
faults.text: Stand tall — don’t lean into the wall

faults.label: Shoulder shrugging
faults.text: Shoulder down, away from the ear
faults.deep: The shoulder is up by your ear — let it drop, and come down the wall if you have to

settings.label: Arm angle that counts as under way
